a_{n}=\sum_{k=1}^{2n-1}k^{-1}\sim\log n,$

so that

$E[\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}]
 =\frac{E[S_{\rm obs}]}{a_{n}L}
 =\theta+\frac{\log(1-d)}{a_{n}L}\to\theta$,
$n\to\infty$.

For any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ and $d^{k}\to0$, i.e. ${\rm Pr}\{$site
lost$\}=d^{k}\to0$.  The $O(1)$ loss $-\theta\log(1-d)$ is $o(a_{n})$.
With the stated “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ the
ascertained site set is retained in the limit and the presence/absence
statistic $S$ on which Watterson’s $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ rests is recovered
asymptotically. The finite $n$ shortfall is $O(1)/a_{n}$ and vanishes for
arbitrarily large $n$.

Nucleotide diversity is frequency weighted.  $E[p_{\rm obs}\mid p]=(1-d)p<p$,
so that

$E[\pi_{\rm site}^{\rm obs}\mid p]=2E[p_{\rm obs}(1-p_{\rm obs})]
<2p(1-p)=\pi_{\rm site}^{\rm true}$,

and in the rare allele regime

$E[\pi_{\rm obs}]=(1-d)\,\pi_{\rm true}+o(1)<\pi_{\rm true}$,

even as $n\to\infty$.  Reference imputation permanently thins derived copies
by the constant factor $1-d$; the expected number of pairwise differences
per site is systematically deflated and the bias does not vanish with
sample size.

Hence on the ascertained VCF set $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ is asymptotically
consistent under random per-sample deletion + missing-as-reference
imputation, whereas $\pi$ is persistently downward biased by the one-way
reference thinning.  Strictly for any finite $n$ $E[S_{\rm obs}]<S_{\rm true}$
so $S$ and $\theta_{W}$ are downward biased by $O(1)/a_{n}$, the classic
finite-sample rare-variant loss, which is negligible in the arbitrarily
large $n$ limit stated.

B. Only $\pi$ is biased; Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically
unbiased on the ascertained site set.

6.text:
The VCF defines the ascertained set of truly segregating SNVs and “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ is the ascertainment condition.  Let $d>0$ be the per haplotype per site probability that a true derived call is filtered and then imputed to reference.  A true reference copy is never changed.

For a true site with $k\ge1$ derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes

* $k'\sim {\rm Bin}\!\left(k,1-d\right)$ is the number of derived copies that survive,
  $E[k'|k]=k(1-d)$,
* $E[p_{obs}|p]=(1-d)p<p$,
* the site is seen as segregating on the imputed matrix iff $k'>0$,

${\rm Pr}\{ {\rm loss}\mid k\}=d^{\,k}$,
$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{j}\left[1-d^{k_{j}}\right]=S_{true}-\sum_{j}d^{k_{j}}$.

On the infinite sites spectrum $E[\#\{k\}]=\theta/k$ so that

$E[S_{obs}]=\theta\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{1-d^{k}}{k}
          =\theta a_{n}+\theta\log(1-d)$,

$a_{n}=\sum_{i=1}^{2n-1}1/i\sim\log n$. The absolute loss
$-\theta\log(1-d)=\sum_{k}d^{k}/k$ is $O(1)$ whereas $S_{true}=\theta a_{n}+o(a_{n})$.
Hence

$E[\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}]
 =\frac{E[S_{obs}]}{a_{n}L}
 =\theta+\frac{\log(1-d)}{a_{n}L}\longrightarrow\theta$

as $n\to\infty$. For any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ and $d^{k}\to0$, so
${\rm Pr}\{k'>0\}\to1$. With the stated ascertainment the indicator of segregation is recovered in the arbitrarily large $n$ limit; the $O(1)$ rare-tail loss is $o(a_{n})$ and vanishes relative to $S$.

Pi is frequency weighted.  In expectation

$E\bigl[2p_{obs}(1-p_{obs})\mid p\bigr]
 =2(1-d)p\bigl[1-(1-d)p\bigr] < 2p(1-p)$

pointwise.  The one-way reference imputation permanently thins the derived
copy number by the constant factor $1-d$; for the rare alleles that dominate
the spectrum

$E[\pi_{site}^{obs}]\approx2(1-d)p$,

so that in the large $n$ limit

$E[\pi_{obs}]=(1-d)\,\pi_{true}+o(1)<\pi_{true}$,

a persistent multiplicative deflation. Pairwise differences are attenuated
at every site and the bias does not vanish with $n$.

Thus on the ascertained VCF set the presence/absence statistic $S/a_{n}$
on which Watterson’s estimator is based is asymptotically recovered, whereas
nucleotide diversity is systematically downward biased by the missing-as-reference
imputation.  In the $n\to\infty$ regime stated this is the usual robustness of
$S$-based $\theta_{W}$ versus the sensitivity of $\pi$.

B. Only pi is biased, Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased for the ascertained set.

9.text:
The VCF defines the ascertained set of sites. Let $d>0$ be the per-haplotype
per-site probability that a true derived call is quality filtered and then
reference imputed. A true reference copy is never changed.

For a true site with $k\ge 1$ derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes
$p=k/2n$,

$k' \sim {\rm Bin}(k,1-d)$,  $E[k'\mid k]=k(1-d)$,
$E[p_{obs}\mid p]=(1-d)p<p$,

and the site is seen as segregating on the imputed matrix iff $k'>0$,

${\rm Pr}\{ {\rm loss}\mid k\}=d^{\,k}$,
${\rm Pr}\{ {\rm seen}\mid k\}=1-d^{\,k}$.

Hence on the ascertained union

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_j[1-d^{k_j}]=S_{true}-\sum_j d^{k_j}$.

With the infinite sites spectrum $E[\#\{k\}]=\theta/k$,
$E[S_{obs}]=\theta\sum_{k\ge1}(1-d^{k})/k
          =\theta a_n+\theta\log(1-d)$,
$a_n=\sum_{1}^{2n-1}1/i\sim\log n$.
The absolute loss $\theta\sum d^{k}/k=-\theta\log(1-d)$ is $O(1)$ whereas
$S_{true}= \theta a_n+o(a_n)$.

For any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and
$d^{k}\to0$. With the stated “no completely missing SNV across all
samples’’ ascertainment the indicator of segregation is recovered in
probability, $S_{obs}\to S_{true}$, and

$E[\hat\theta_W^{obs}]=E[S_{obs}]/a_n
 =\theta+\frac{\log(1-d)}{a_n}\longrightarrow\theta,$

up to the usual ascertainment to the VCF set. The $O(1)$ rare-tail loss is
$o(a_n)$ and is negligible for arbitrarily large $n$. $S/a_n$ is a
presence/absence statistic and is asymptotically insensitive to the
one-way reference thinning.

Nucleotide diversity is frequency weighted. The observed derived
frequency is permanently thinned,

$E[p_{obs}\mid p]=(1-d)p$,

so that point-wise

$E[2p_{obs}(1-p_{obs})\mid p]=2(1-d)p[1-(1-d)p]<2p(1-p)$.

In the rare-allele regime that dominates the spectrum
$E[\pi_{site}^{obs}]\approx2(1-d)p$ and

$E[\pi_{obs}]=(1-d)\,\pi_{true}+o(1)<\pi_{true}$

even as $n\to\infty$. Reference imputation can only turn true derived
copies into reference copies, so the average number of pairwise differences
per site is attenuated by the constant factor $1-d$ and the bias does not
vanish with sample size.

Hence on the ascertained SNV set Watterson’s $S/a_n$ is asymptotically
consistent while $\pi$ remains systematically downward biased by the
missing-as-reference imputation.

B. Only pi is biased, Watterson’s theta is asymptotically unbiased in the
arbitrarily large $n$ limit; in any finite $n$ there is the usual
$O(1)/a_n$ downward finite-sample loss of $S$ which is the source of the
both-biased view.

Let d>0 be the per-haplotype per-site probability that a true derived call is filtered out and then imputed to reference. A true reference copy is never changed. For a true site with k≥1 derived copies in 2n haplotypes k′ ∼ Bin(k,1−d) , E[k′|k]=k(1−d) is the number of derived copies that survive in the imputed matrix. The site is seen as segregating in the imputed data iff k′>0 Pr{ observed segregating | k}=1−d^{k}. Hence with k_{j} the true derived copy number at site j E[S_{obs}] = Σ_{j}[1−d^{k_{j}}] = S_{true}−Σ_{j}d^{k_{j}} . So E[θ_{W}^{obs}] = E[S_{obs}]/{a_{n}L}= θ + log(1−d)/a_{n}L and Pr{loss|k}=d^{k}→0 for every fixed p>0 as k=2np→∞. 8.text:
The imputed data are a genotype independent thinning of the true derived
alleles followed by a one way reference imputation

* derived → derived with prob $1-d$
* derived → reference with prob $d$,
* reference → reference with prob 1.

For a true site with $k\ge 1$ derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes
$k' \sim {\rm Bin}(k,1-d)$, $E[k'\mid k]=k(1-d)$ and

${\rm Pr}\{k'>0\mid k\}=1-d^{\,k}\;.$

Hence on the ascertained VCF set

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{j}\!\left[1-d^{k_{j}}\right]
          =S_{true}-\sum_{j}d^{k_{j}}.$

On the infinite sites spectrum $E[\#\{k\}] \propto\theta/k$,

$E[S_{obs}]
  =\theta\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{1-d^{k}}{k}
  =\theta a_{n}+\theta\log(1-d), \qquad 
  a_{n}=\sum_{1}^{2n-1}k^{-1}\sim\log n.$

The loss $\sum d^{k}/k=-\log(1-d)=O(1)$ whereas $a_{n}\to\infty$.
For any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ and $d^{\,k}\to0$, so a truly
segregating ascertained site is lost with probability $1-d^{k}\to1$.
In particular

$E\!\left[\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}\right]
   =\frac{E[S_{obs}]}{a_{n}L}
   =\theta+\frac{\log(1-d)}{a_{n}L}\longrightarrow\theta,$

$n\to\infty$, i.e. up to the $O(1)/a_{n}$ rare-tail term the presence/absence
statistic $S$ and $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ is recovered asymptotically on the
ascertained variant set.  The $O(1)$ absolute loss $-\theta\log(1-d)$ is
$o(a_{n})$ and vanishes relative to $S$ for arbitrarily large $n$.

$\pi$ is frequency weighted.  With $E[p_{obs}\mid p]=(1-d)p<p$,

$E\!\left[\pi_{site}^{obs}\mid p\right]
 =2E[p_{obs}(1-p_{obs})]
 =2(1-d)p\,[1-(1-d)p]
 <2p(1-p)=\pi_{site}^{true}$

pointwise, and in the large $n$ limit

$E[\pi_{obs}]=(1-d)\,\pi_{true}+o(1)<\pi_{true},$

i.e. the one way reference imputation permanently thins the derived
copy number by the constant factor $1-d$.  Pairwise differences are
therefore systematically deflated whereas the segregating site count on
which Watterson’s estimator rests is asymptotically preserved.  This is
the usual robustness of the $S/a_{n}$ statistic to random
missing-as-reference versus the persistent downward bias of nucleotide
diversity.

In the arbitrarily large-sample limit therefore $\theta_{W}$ is
asymptotically essentially unbiased for the ascertained VCF set while
$\pi$ remains persistently downward biased. ∎

I’m leaning toward both statistics being deflated by the missing-as-reference step, and that’s why I’m not comfortable calling Watterson asymptotically clean in the way it’s usually used here.

Reference imputation is one-way: a true derived copy that is filtered is forced to reference, a true reference is never turned into derived. So for any site the observed derived count is a thinned version of the true count. In expectation E[p̂|p]=(1−d)p < p with per-haplotype deletion probability d>0. That is why π is unambiguously downward biased, 2E[p̂(1−p̂)] < 2p(1−p), and the attenuation factor is essentially 1−d for the copy number that contributes to pairwise differences. That part is agreed.

The same thinning hits S. A true site with k ≥1 derived copies is observed as segregating in the imputed matrix only if k′>0 where k′∼Bin(k,1−d). The site loss probability is d^{k} and E[Î]=1−d^{k}<1 for every finite k. Hence

E[Ŝ]= Σ_{j}[1−d^{k_j}] = S_true − Σ_{j} d^{k_j} < S_true.

With the infinite-sites spectrum E[#k]=θ/k the absolute shortfall is Σ d^{k}/k = −log(1−d) >0, i.e. a constant O(1) loss in segregating sites. Singletons are lost with probability d, doubletons with d², etc., and the spectrum is dominated by rare alleles.

The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition refers to the pre-filter VCF, not to the post-imputation matrix we actually compute on. After random per-sample quality filtering a true segregating site can be rendered apparently fixed reference when all of its carriers happen to be filtered in that sample and are imputed to reference. Reference imputation can never create a new segregating site, it can only erase evidence of the derived allele.

It is true that for a fixed frequency p>0, k=2np→∞ and d^{k}→0, so the relative loss is o(a_n). Dividing by a_n∼log n gives E[θ_Ŵ]=θ+log(1−d)/a_n, which tends to θ in the strict n→∞ limit. Consistency is not unbiasedness. For any finite, and for any practically achievable “arbitrarily large’’ sample with a substantial minority d>0, the term log(1−d)/a_n is still >0 and the rare-allele tail that dominates S contributes a non-vanishing absolute loss. The estimator we actually calculate on the reference-imputed haplotypes is systematically low.

Because both the site-presence indicator and the frequency-weighted pairwise difference are built from the same thinned derived counts, both Watterson’s S/a_n and π are attenuated by the one-way reference imputation. In practice we get a downward bias in both statistics, not just in π.

I’m staying with both-biased for the data we actually compute on, and I think the B-camp asymptotic story hides the operational bias.

Reference imputation after per-sample quality filtering is strictly one-way: a true derived allele is seen as derived only when it survives the filter, with per-haplotype survival 1−d, and a filtered derived copy is forced to reference. A true reference copy is never turned into derived. So the observed derived count at a true site with k true derived copies is thinned, E[k′|k]=k(1−d), and the site is scored as segregating in the imputed matrix only if k′>0.

That means a site can be made apparently monomorphic reference when the small set of carriers happen to be filtered in their samples. The loss probability for the site is d^k >0 for every finite k. The infinite-sites spectrum puts weight ∝θ/k on each k, so rare alleles dominate S. Singletons are lost with probability d, doubletons with d², etc. With a substantial minority d>0 the expected shortfall in the segregating-site count is Σj d^{k_j}= θ Σ d^k/k = −θ log(1−d) >0, an O(1) absolute loss that does not depend on n. The condition “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ is an ascertainment condition on the original VCF, not a guarantee that segregation is preserved after per-sample random deletion and reference imputation.

Hence E[S_obs] < S_true for any finite, practically achievable “arbitrarily large’’ sample, and θ_W = S_obs / a_n is computed on that downward-thinned S. The a_n∼log n normalisation grows, but the bias in S is a constant, not a vanishing relative error in practice; we are estimating θ on the reference-imputed haplotypes we actually have, not on the n→∞ limit.

π is hit even more transparently. The per-site observed derived frequency is E[p̂|p]=(1−d)p<p, so the expected per-site contribution 2p̂(1−p̂) is strictly <2p(1−p). Pairwise differences are thinned by the same one-way erasure of derived copies, giving a persistent multiplicative attenuation ~1−d that does not disappear with sample size.

Reference imputation can never create polymorphism, it can only erase evidence of the derived allele. Both the presence/absence statistic S on which Watterson rests and the frequency-weighted statistic π are therefore attenuated downward on the imputed sequences we analyse. That is the systematic deflation we should report.

6.text:
Reference imputation after per-sample quality filtering is a one-way thinning of
derived copies.

Let $d>0$ be the per haplotype per site probability that a true derived call
is filtered and then forced to reference. A true reference copy is never
changed.  On the ascertained VCF set let a true site have $k\ge 1$ derived
copies in $2n$ haplotypes, $p=k/2n$.

$k'\sim{\rm Bin}\!\left(k,1-d\right)$ is the number of derived copies that
survive in the imputed matrix,
${\rm E}[k'|k]=k(1-d)$ and

${\rm Pr}\{k'>0\mid k\}=1-d^{\,k}$.

The site is seen as segregating in the imputed matrix iff $k'>0$. Hence

${\rm E}[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{j}\bigl[1-d^{k_{j}}\bigr]
      =S_{\rm true}-\sum_{j}d^{k_{j}}<S_{\rm true}$

for any finite $n$.  On the infinite-sites spectrum
${\rm E}[\#k]=\theta/k$,

${\rm E}[S_{\rm obs}]
 =\theta\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{1-d^{k}}{k}
 =\theta a_{n}+\theta\log(1-d)$,
$a_{n}=\sum_{1}^{2n-1}k^{-1}\sim\log n$,

so that

${\rm E}[\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}]
 =\frac{{\rm E}[S_{\rm obs}]}{a_{n}L}
 =\theta+\frac{\log(1-d)}{a_{n}L}\to\theta$,
$n\to\infty$.

For any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ and $d^{k}\to0$,
${\rm Pr}\{{\rm site\;lost}\}=d^{k}\to0$.  With the stated
“no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ ascertainment the set of
ascertained sites is retained in the limit and the $O(1)$ absolute loss
$-\theta\log(1-d)$ is $o(a_{n})$.  $S/a_{n}$ is a presence/absence
statistic; up to the usual $O(1)/a_{n}$ rare-tail term Watterson’s
$\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically recovered on the ascertained variant set
under random missing-as-reference thinning.  The finite-$n$ shortfall is
$\log(1-d)/a_{n}<0$ and vanishes for arbitrarily large $n$.

Nucleotide diversity is frequency weighted.  ${\rm E}[p_{\rm obs}\mid p]
 =(1-d)p<p$, and

${\rm E}[\pi_{\rm site}^{\rm obs}\mid p]
 =2{\rm E}[p_{\rm obs}(1-p_{\rm obs})]
 =2(1-d)p\bigl[1-(1-d)p\bigr]<2p(1-p)$

pointwise.  In the rare-allele regime that dominates $\pi$,

${\rm E}[\pi_{\rm obs}]
 =(1-d)\,\pi_{\rm true}+o(1)<\pi_{\rm true}$,

even as $n\to\infty$.  A filtered derived copy is permanently turned into
a reference copy; the average number of pairwise differences per site is
attenuated by the constant factor $1-d$.  The bias does not vanish with
sample size.

Hence on the ascertained VCF set $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ is asymptotically
consistent under random per-sample deletion + missing-as-reference
imputation, whereas $\pi$ is persistently downward biased by the one-way
reference thinning.  In the arbitrarily large-$n$ limit intended by the
statement the bias is effectively confined to $\pi$.

B. Only $\pi$ is persistently biased; Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$ is
asymptotically unbiased/consistent on the ascertained set, with the
usual $O(1)/a_{n}$ finite-sample rare-allele downward term that is
$o(1)$ for arbitrarily large $n$.

3.text:
Missing-as-reference after random per-sample quality filtering is a one-way
thinning of the derived allele.

Let $d>0$ be the per-haplotype per-site probability that a true derived call
is filtered and then forced to reference. A true reference copy is never
changed. For a true site with $k\ge 1$ derived copies in $2n$ haplotypes

$k'\sim{\rm Bin}(k,1-d)$, $E[k'|k]=k(1-d)$,
$E[p_{obs}|p]=(1-d)p<p$,

and the site is scored as segregating on the imputed matrix iff $k'>0$,

${\rm Pr}\{{\rm seen}\mid k\}=1-d^{\,k}$, ${\rm Pr}\{{\rm loss}\mid k\}=d^{\,k}$.

On the ascertained union VCF set

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_j[1-d^{k_j}]=S_{true}-\sum_j d^{k_j}<S_{true}$.

With the infinite sites spectrum $E[\#k]=\theta/k$

$E[S_{obs}]=\theta\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{1-d^{k}}{k}
          =\theta a_n+\theta\log(1-d)$,

$a_n=\sum_{1}^{2n-1}1/k\sim\log n$.
Hence

$E[\hat\theta_W^{obs}]
 =\frac{E[S_{obs}]}{a_nL}
 =\theta+\frac{\log(1-d)}{a_nL}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\theta$.

The absolute loss $-\theta\log(1-d)=\theta\sum_k d^k/k$ is $O(1)$ while
$S_{true}= \theta a_n+o(a_n)$. For any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ and

SNV ascertainment the indicator of segregation is recovered in the limit
and the $O(1)/a_n$ rare-tail loss of $S/a_n$ is $o(1)$ for arbitrarily large
$n$. $S/a_n$ is a presence/absence statistic and is asymptotically recovered
on the ascertained site set.

$\pi$ is frequency weighted. Pointwise

$E[p_{obs}\mid p]=(1-d)p$,

$E[\pi_{site}^{obs}\mid p]=2E[p_{obs}(1-p_{obs})]
   =2(1-d)p[1-(1-d)p]<2p(1-p)$.

In the rare allele regime that dominates $\pi$

$E[\pi_{obs}]=(1-d)\,\pi_{true}+o(1)<\pi_{true}$,

even as $n\to\infty$. A filtered derived copy is permanently turned into a
reference copy, so the expected number of pairwise differences per site is

Reference imputation after per-sample quality filtering is a one-way thinning of
derived copies.

Let $d>0$ be the per haplotype per site probability that a true derived call
is filtered and then forced to reference. A true reference copy is never
changed.  On the ascertained VCF set let a true site have $k\ge 1$ derived
copies in $2n$ haplotypes, $p=k/2n$.

$k'\sim{\rm Bin}\!\left(k,1-d\right)$ is the number of derived copies that
survive in the imputed matrix,
${\rm E}[k'|k]=k(1-d)$ and

${\rm Pr}\{k'>0\mid k\}=1-d^{\,k}$.

The site is seen as segregating in the imputed matrix iff $k'>0$. Hence

${\rm E}[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{j}\bigl[1-d^{k_{j}}\bigr]
      =S_{\rm true}-\sum_{j}d^{k_{j}}<S_{\rm true}$

for any finite $n$.  On the infinite-sites spectrum
${\rm E}[\#k]=\theta/k$,

${\rm E}[S_{\rm obs}]
 =\theta\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{1-d^{k}}{k}
 =\theta a_{n}+\theta\log(1-d)$,
$a_{n}=\sum_{1}^{2n-1}k^{-1}\sim\log n$,

so that

${\rm E}[\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}]
 =\frac{{\rm E}[S_{\rm obs}]}{a_{n}L}
 =\theta+\frac{\log(1-d)}{a_{n}L}\to\theta$,
$n\to\infty$.

For any fixed $p>0$, $k=2np\to\infty$ and $d^{k}\to0$,
${\rm Pr}\{{\rm site\;lost}\}=d^{k}\to0$.  With the stated
“no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ ascertainment the set of
ascertained sites is retained in the limit and the $O(1)$ absolute loss
$-\theta\log(1-d)$ is $o(a_{n})$.  $S/a_{n}$ is a presence/absence
statistic; up to the usual $O(1)/a_{n}$ rare-tail term Watterson’s
$\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically recovered on the ascertained variant set
under random missing-as-reference thinning.  The finite-$n$ shortfall is
$\log(1-d)/a_{n}<0$ and vanishes for arbitrarily large $n$.

Nucleotide diversity is frequency weighted.  ${\rm E}[p_{\rm obs}\mid p]
 =(1-d)p<p$, and

${\rm E}[\pi_{\rm site}^{\rm obs}\mid p]
 =2{\rm E}[p_{\rm obs}(1-p_{\rm obs})]
 =2(1-d)p\bigl[1-(1-d)p\bigr]<2p(1-p)$

pointwise.  In the rare-allele regime that dominates $\pi$,

${\rm E}[\pi_{\rm obs}]
 =(1-d)\,\pi_{\rm true}+o(1)<\pi_{\rm true}$,

even as $n\to\infty$.  A filtered derived copy is permanently turned into
a reference copy; the average number of pairwise differences per site is
attenuated by the constant factor $1-d$.  The bias does not vanish with
sample size.

Hence on the ascertained VCF set $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ is asymptotically
consistent under random per-sample deletion + missing-as-reference
imputation, whereas $\pi$ is persistently downward biased by the one-way
reference thinning.  In the arbitrarily large-$n$ limit intended by the
statement the bias is effectively confined to $\pi$.

B. Only $\pi$ is persistently biased; Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$ is
asymptotically unbiased/consistent on the ascertained set, with the
usual $O(1)/a_{n}$ finite-sample rare-allele downward term that is
$o(1)$ for arbitrarily large $n$.

Reference imputation after per sample quality filtering is a one way thinning

is filtered and then imputed to reference. A true reference copy is never
changed.  On the union VCF set let a true site have $k\ge1$ derived copies in
$2n$ chromosomes. After filtering + missing as reference

$k'\sim{\rm Bin}(k,1-d),\qquad E[k'|k]=k(1-d),\qquad 
E[p_{obs}|p]=(1-d)p<p,$

and the site is scored as segregating on the imputed matrix iff $k'>0$,

${\rm Pr}\{{\rm seen}\mid k\}=1-d^{k},\qquad {\rm Pr}\{{\rm loss}\mid k\}=d^{k}$.

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{j}\bigl[1-d^{k_{j}}\bigr]=S_{true}-\sum_{j}d^{k_{j}}<S_{true}$.

$E[S_{obs}]=\theta\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{1-d^{k}}{k}
          =\theta a_{n}+\theta\log(1-d)$,
$a_{n}=\sum_{1}^{2n-1}k^{-1}\sim\log n$,

$E[\hat\theta_{W}^{obs}]
 =\frac{E[S_{obs}]}{a_{n}L}
 =\theta+\frac{\log(1-d)}{a_{n}L}\to\theta,\qquad n\to\infty$.

on the ascertained VCF set. The $O(1)/a_{n}=O(1)/\log n$ rare tail shortfall
$\log(1-d)/a_{n}<0$ is $o(1)$ for arbitrarily large $n$.

Nucleotide diversity is frequency weighted. Pointwise

$E[\pi_{site}^{obs}\mid p]
 =2E[p_{obs}(1-p_{obs})]

The per-sample quality filter is one-way thinning of derived copies. With per-haplotype per-site deletion / reference-imputation probability d>0, a true site with k≥1 derived copies in 2n haplotypes has k′∼Bin(k,1−d), E[k′|k]=k(1−d), E[p_obs|p]=(1−d)p<p. A true reference copy is never changed. Site is scored segregating on the imputed matrix iff k′>0, Pr{seen|k}=1−d^{k}, Pr{loss|k}=d^{k}. Hence E[S_obs]=∑[1−d^{k_j}]=S_true−∑d^{k_j}<S_true for any finite n.

On infinite sites E[#k]=θ/k,
E[S_obs]=θ∑(1−d^{k})/k=θ a_n+θ log(1−d), a_n=∑_{1}^{2n−1}1/k∼log n.
Thus E[θ̂_W^{obs}]=E[S_obs]/(a_n L)=θ+log(1−d)/(a_n L). The absolute loss −θ log(1−d)=θ∑d^{k}/k is O(1); the relative loss is O(1)/a_n→0 as n→∞. For fixed p>0, k=2np→∞ so d^{k}→0 and Pr{loss|k}→0. With the “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ ascertainment the set of ascertained sites is retained in probability and S_obs/S_true→1. S/a_n is a presence/absence statistic and is asymptotically recovered.

In the rare-allele regime E[π_obs]≈(1−d)π_true and more generally E[π_obs]=(1−d)π_true+o(1)<π_true even as n→∞. Pairwise differences are attenuated by the constant factor 1−d; the bias persists in the large-n limit.
